question: A crash-test buggy of mass 21000 g moves at a speed, in m/s, equal to 3 times the sum of 6 and 14. The buggy's wheelbase is 1.4 m. From its energy of motion subtract 3 J lost to rolling resistance; 2 identical buggies are run, so double the result and express it in kJ. The test is repeated for 3 identical rounds and the round totals are added. What is the final total, in kJ?

The quantity to report is a total energy in kJ for 8 identical pods, each contributing its energy of motion in kJ. A pod has a mass of 52000 g. Its speed, in m/s, is the sum of the terms 2k − 1 for k running from 1 to 8, reduced by 10. Find one pod's energy of motion, convert it to kJ, and scale to the 8 pods. What is the total, in kJ?

A conveyor in a quarry pushes hoppers, each of mass 57 kg, at an acceleration, in m/s², equal to 4 times the sum of 8 and 6, less 11. The belt runs at 32 °C. The force on one hopper is what is required to give it that acceleration, and 3 hoppers are pushed together. To the combined force add 11 N from a guide-rail spring, then subtract 22 N of belt friction. What is the resulting force, in N?

A mine locomotive hauls ore skips, each of mass 146 kg, and gives every skip an acceleration, in m/s², equal to the sum of k for k running from 1 to 9. The force on one skip is the force needed to produce that acceleration. Skips are coupled in pairs, so a coupling carries the force for 2 skips, less 26 N absorbed by the coupling's own damper; express a coupling's force in kN. The train has 12 such couplings, all loaded identically. What is the total force over the 12 couplings, in kN?

The figure a bakery engineer needs is a total energy in kJ for 12 identical oven conveyor lines, each line's figure being the energy of its 12 identical trays converted to kJ. Each tray's energy is its energy of motion plus 7 J stored in its spring-loaded latch. A tray has a mass of 13 kg and moves at a speed, in m/s, equal to the number of ways of choosing 3 slots out of 6. Work out one tray, then the 12 trays of a line in kJ, then the 12 lines. What is the total, in kJ?

The total a test director wants is an energy in J for 6 identical test batches, each batch made of 12 identical launches, where each launch's figure is a sled's energy of motion plus 28 J from an ejector spring. The sled has a mass of 26 kg. It starts from rest at t = 2 s, and from t = 2 s to t = 3 s its acceleration, in m/s², is 2t² + 3t with t in seconds; its energy of motion is taken at its speed at t = 3 s. What is the total for the 6 batches, in J?

A lab-bench cart of mass 37 kg is released from rest at t = 0 s, and from t = 0 s to t = 1 s its acceleration, in m/s², is 1t² + 0t with t in seconds. At t = 1 s a launcher multiplies the cart's speed by 9. Find the cart's energy of motion at the boosted speed and express it in kJ. 9 identical carts are treated this way and their energies added, and then 10 kJ consumed by the launcher's compressor is subtracted, energy gained counting positive and energy consumed negative. What is the resulting signed energy balance, in kJ?

The number required is a total energy in kJ for 8 identical shuttle runs, each run's figure being a shuttle's remaining energy in kJ. A shuttle has a mass of 21 kg and runs at a speed, in m/s, equal to 2 times the sum of 5 and 11. From its energy of motion subtract 9 J lost in the wheel bearings and then 8 J lost to air drag to get the remaining energy, then convert to kJ. What is the total for the 8 runs, in kJ?

A cart of mass 72000 g is accelerated along a bench at a rate, in m/s², equal to the largest whole number that divides both 165 and 48 with no remainder. The force needed for that acceleration is expressed in kN and taken as positive in the direction of motion. An 18 kN retarding force then acts against it, after which a 7 kN assisting push acts along it. What is the resulting signed net force, in kN?

The quantity wanted is a signed net force in kN, forward positive: the combined pull of 7 identical winches, minus a 15 kN retarding load. Each winch drives 6 identical carts, and each cart has a mass of 34000 g and is accelerated at a, in m/s², where a is the smaller of the two values satisfying a² − 13a + 42 = 0. The pull on one cart is the force required to give it that acceleration, expressed in kN; a winch's pull is that of its 6 carts combined. What is the net signed force, in kN?

The total a test manager needs is an energy in kJ: the combined energy of motion of all the pucks in 8 identical racks, plus 21 J from a spring launcher, with the sum converted to kJ. Each rack holds 12 identical pucks. A puck has a mass of 53000 g and slides at a speed, in m/s, equal to the number of ways of choosing 2 markers out of 9. The rink is kept at −4 °C. Find one puck's energy, then a rack's, then the 8 racks', before adding the launcher's contribution. What is the total, in kJ?

A dockside crane accelerates a container of mass 76000 g at a rate, in m/s², equal to the largest whole number that divides both 67 and 21 with no remainder, plus 10. The crane's boom is 32 m long. The lifting force beyond the container's weight is what is needed for that acceleration; express it in kN and take upward as positive. The crane runs 5 identical lifts and their forces are added, after which a 16 kN downward load from a snagged sling is subtracted. What is the resulting signed force, in kN?

The quantity to find is a total energy in kJ for 11 identical drones, each contributing its energy of motion less 1 J of rotor-hub friction. A drone has a mass of 44000 g. Starting from rest at t = 3 s, its acceleration from t = 3 s to t = 4 s is 2t² + 2t, in m/s², with t in seconds; at t = 4 s a boost doubles its speed, and the energy of motion is taken at the doubled speed. Add up the 11 drones' contributions in J and convert to kJ. What is the total, in kJ?

A bead of mass 2 kg slides on a lab-bench rail 0.9 m long. It starts from rest at t = 2 s, and from t = 2 s to t = 3 s its acceleration, in m/s², is 4t² + 5t with t in seconds. Take its energy of motion at its speed at t = 3 s, add 22 J from a magnetic kick, and express the result in kJ. 11 identical beads are run this way, and the experiment is repeated 10 times. What is the total energy over all beads and repeats, in kJ?

A hospital bed of mass 99000 g is pushed with an acceleration, in m/s², equal to the largest whole number that divides both 381 and 245 with no remainder. The corridor is 45 m long. The push needed for that acceleration is increased by 22 N to overcome castor friction and then by a further 4 N for a door threshold. What is the total push, in kN?

A conveyor arm of mass 15 kg has position 3t³ − 1t² metres along its rail, with t in seconds. The arm's motor is rated at 240 V. The force on the arm is what is needed to give it the acceleration it has at t = 4 s. A machine has 8 such arms, a plant has 9 such machines, and there are 2 identical plants. What is the total force over both plants, in kN?

A toy car of mass 14000 g starts from rest at t = 0 s and from t = 0 s to t = 1 s its acceleration, in m/s², is 1t² + 6t with t in seconds. The track is 4.5 m long. Take the car's energy of motion at its speed at t = 1 s and add 16 J from its wound spring. 2 cars race at once, and the club holds 6 identical races. What is the total energy over all the races, in J?

A dolly of mass 57000 g is pushed with an acceleration a, in m/s², where a is the larger of the two values satisfying a² − 7a + 12 = 0. The dolly is 1.1 m long. From the push required for that acceleration, 27 N is absorbed by floor friction and then a further 6 N by the castor bearings. What is the force that remains, in kN?

A slot car of mass 59000 g has position 1t³ + 5t² metres along its track, with t in seconds. The track is 18 m long. Find the car's energy of motion at its speed at t = 3 s and express it in kJ. A lane runs 6 such cars, a track has 4 such lanes, and the venue has 11 such tracks. What is the total energy, in kJ?

A forklift on a warehouse floor pushes a pallet of mass 128000 g. The pallet's acceleration, in m/s², is 5 times a, where a is the smaller of the two values satisfying a² − 7a + 10 = 0. The forklift's mast is 3.2 m tall. Express the push required for that acceleration in kN. The warehouse operates 5 identical forklifts pushing identical pallets at once. What is their combined push, in kN?

The result the lab wants is a signed net force in kN, forward positive: a probe's forward force converted to kN, minus a 14 kN retarding clamp. The probe has a mass of 2 kg and sits on a bench 1.6 m wide. Its acceleration, in m/s², is 11 times the largest whole number that divides both 206 and 325 with no remainder. The forward force is what is needed to produce that acceleration, plus a 4 N push from a spring. What is the net signed force, in kN?

A trolley of mass 87000 g is pushed with an acceleration a, in m/s², where a is the smaller of the two values satisfying a² − 10a + 16 = 0. The push needed for that acceleration is increased by 7 N for castor friction and then by 20 N for a ramp. The trolley's handle is 0.9 m high. 11 identical trolleys are pushed this way and their pushes are added, and then an 8 N reading offset is added. What is the final figure, in N?

A cart of mass 25000 g starts with zero acceleration at t = 0 s, and its acceleration grows at a rate of 2t² + 8t, in m/s³, with t in seconds, until t = 3 s. The bench is 2.0 m long. The force on the cart is what is needed to give it the acceleration reached at t = 3 s; express it in kN and take it as positive. 8 identical carts are pushed together and their forces added, after which an 8 kN retarding force and then a 29 kN braking force act against them. What is the resulting signed net force, in kN?

The figure a launch crew wants is a final energy in kJ: the energy of motion of 9 identical capsules, converted to kJ, minus 29 kJ spent on separation charges, plus 13 kJ recovered by a brake. Each capsule has a mass of 40000 g and moves at a speed, in m/s, equal to the number of ways of choosing 4 seats out of 7. Find one capsule's energy first and scale to the 9 capsules before converting. What is the final energy, in kJ?

A skateboard of mass 52 kg on the test bench moves at a speed v, in m/s, where v is the larger of the two values satisfying v² − 3v + 2 = 0. The board's deck is 0.8 m long. To its energy of motion add 18 J from a push, then 14 J from a second push. 7 identical boards are treated this way and their energies added, then 13 J from a final nudge is added. What is the total, in J?
